data.narrative:
Built Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing automation company founded by Noah Ready-Campbell and Andrew Liang, has raised $112M+ to date. The valuation analysis triangulates across a peer set of nine private companies and one public comparable in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including stage-adjacent firms like Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), Bedrock Robotics (Series B, $1.8B), Hadrian (Series D, $1.6B), and Dexterity (Series B, $1.6B).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $400M implied value proxy of total capital raised, applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $680M. Peer-median benchmarking across seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a peer range of $1.0B to $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $578M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $1.2B. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around stage-specific progression rates and the heterogeneity of robotics subsectors represented in the peer set. Key sensitivities include the timing and terms of Series D fundraising and revenue traction relative to manufacturing automation peers.
